headline: Axiom Executive Arrested as Sterling-Nakamura Hands Tribunal 40TB of Stolen Trade Data
body:
Federal Remnant arbitration tribunal seated in The Spires this morning accepted a 40-terabyte evidence package from Sterling-Nakamura's legal division documenting what the corponation describes as a three-year systematic intelligence operation by Axiom against its quantum materials research program. Axiom's Chief Intelligence Liaison, Brenn Vasquez-Obi, was taken into Federal custody at 0730 as part of a coordinated sweep that also detained four contractors believed to have served as data couriers. The stolen material allegedly includes proprietary formulations for Sterling-Nakamura's next-generation conductive polymer line — technology that analysts estimate is worth upward of 900 million quanta in licensing value. Axiom has not issued a formal statement as of this broadcast, but sources inside Axiom News Network describe the corponation's communications team as 'in controlled collapse.'

The scale of the alleged operation is what separates this case from routine competitive intelligence skirmishing. Sterling-Nakamura's filing claims Axiom embedded at least two long-term human assets inside Sterling-Nakamura's Circuit District research campus over a period beginning in 2194, supplemented by an external runner network that moved physical data pulls through Geartown's industrial freight corridors to avoid Ferrogate Transit's standard cargo logging. Graycloaks are believed to have brokered at least a portion of the intelligence handoffs, a detail that has made several information broker circles visibly uncomfortable this morning. One source close to the case, speaking anonymously, said the runner network involved 'more familiar names than anyone on either side wants attributed.'

Sterling-Nakamura's decision to go public rather than negotiate a private settlement is being read as a deliberate escalation — a message to the broader corponation landscape about the cost of direct IP theft. Sterling Financial Digest noted this morning that Sterling-Nakamura's polymer division stock position had already been quietly restructured in the 72 hours before the filing went public, suggesting the legal action was at minimum partially coordinated with its financial strategy team. Axiom's share value in the Quanta exchange dropped 6.8% in the first hour of trading.

The Federal Remnant tribunal has set a preliminary hearing for May 9th. Arcturus Defense, which provides security to both corponations in different districts, has issued a statement declaring neutrality — a statement that exactly nobody in The Spires finds credible.
aftermath: Brenn Vasquez-Obi accepted a sealed plea arrangement in September 2197, and Axiom ultimately paid a 340 million quanta settlement to Sterling-Nakamura, though internal Axiom communications leaked by the Graycloaks the following year suggested the corponation considered the settlement a cost of doing business.
runner_relevance: This scandal retroactively burned every runner who had touched the Axiom data operation — several went underground in the Underworld or fled to Old Harbor safe houses the moment the tribunal filing went public. Both corponations began issuing counter-intelligence contracts: Axiom hired runners to identify which members of their own courier network had become liabilities or informants, while Sterling-Nakamura contracted extraction teams to recover any remaining physical data assets still in transit. The Graycloaks, implicated as brokers, quietly offered their own settlement contracts — paying runners to deliver evidence packages to the tribunal that would shift blame away from information broker networks. The case also created a wave of corporate security audit contracts across every major corponation in Meridian 88, all of them looking for their own Axiom-shaped holes.
